title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: GAR Miror Rom. 5 / Deut 29:29; PLAC internal act
pass_a_gloss: GAR wonders why I treat seekers of original corruption's cause—and of birth-penalties on posterity—in first-sin imputation (and so participation) as invaders of God's hidden mind, when he knows ancients and moderns teach that and claim Romans 5 as their source, with many proofs still to come. Branding them all as rash trespassers of the Deuteronomy 29:29 bounds, he doubts, sits ill with fidelity. PLAC: The live issue was that inward divine act said to make God regard all as one man in Adam. Did the ancients and moderns assert that? Does Romans 5 yield it? Did he pile testimonies for it? To credit God with an unscriptural, irrational inward consideration of mind and will—if that is not storming the secret mind, what is?
pass_b_english: GAR. I only marvel by what reason he judges that those who seek the cause of original corruption, and of all the penalties lying upon posterity from birth itself, in the imputation—and so the participation—of the first sin are bursting into God's secret mind, when he is not unaware that older and more recent theologians both teach this and profess that they drew it from the Apostle's doctrine in Romans 5, as will afterward be proved by most frequent testimonies. To press all these with so grave an accusation, as if by rash daring bursting into God's secret mind and crossing those limits which God set for man in Deuteronomy 29:29—I do not know whether it is sufficiently agreeable to faithfulness. PLAC. First the debate was about that inward act of God by which God was said to have considered all men as one man in Adam. Did the older and more recent theologians say that? Can that be gathered from the Apostle's doctrine in Romans 5? Did the learned man bring most frequent testimonies to prove it? To ascribe to God a consideration—a certain inward act of mind and will—beyond Scripture, beyond reason: what is it to burst into God's secret mind, if this is not?
source_text: GAR. Miror solum, qua ratione ductus, eos arbitretur in arcanam Dei mentem irrumpere, qui corruptionis Originalis, & omnium poenarum in posteros ab ipsa nativitate incumbentium causam quaerunt in imputatione, adeoque participatione primi peccati; cum non ignoret veteres & Recentiores Theologos, hoc & docere, & profiteri se hausisse ex Apostoli doctrina Roman. v. Sicut postea frequentissimis testimoniis probabitur. Hos omnes gravissima accusatione urgere, quasi in arcanam Dei mentem temerario ausu irrumpentes, & limites illos transeuntes, quos Deus homini praestituit Deuter. XXIX. 29. nescio an fideciore satis consentaneum sit. PLAC. Primum agebatur de eo Dei actu interno, quo dicebatur Deus omnes homines considerasse tanquam unum hominem in Adamo. Idne veteres & Recentiores Theologi dixerunt? Idne colligi potest ex Apostoli doctrina Roman. v? Attulitne Vir doctus frequentissima testimonia ut id probaret? Tribuere Deo considerationem, actum quendam mentis & voluntatis internum praeter Scripturam, praeter rationem, quid est irrumpere in arcanam Dei mentem, si hoc non est?
